caption_en:
The Swiss one explains something you see every day.

What European countries call themselves:
Germany: Deutschland (from Old High German diutisc, "of the people")
Austria: Österreich ("eastern realm")
Switzerland: Schweiz, Suisse, Svizzera, Svizra. Four official languages, so coins and stamps use the Latin Helvetia, and the country code CH is Confoederatio Helvetica
Hungary: Magyarország ("land of the Magyars")
Finland: Suomi (its origin is uncertain)
Norway: Norge (from Old Norse for "the way north")
Greece: Hellas / Ελλάς (the Romans called them Graeci; Greeks call themselves Hellenes)
Albania: Shqipëria (popularly linked to shqiponjë, eagle, as on the flag)
Croatia: Hrvatska
Montenegro: Crna Gora / Црна Гора (both mean "black mountain")
Ireland: Éire (English "Ireland" is Éire + land)

Neither name is wrong. One is just theirs.

caption_he:
השוויצרית מסבירה משהו שאתם רואים כל יום.

איך מדינות אירופה קוראות לעצמן: גרמניה היא דויטשלנד, אוסטריה היא אסטרייך ("הממלכה המזרחית"), שווייץ היא הלווטיה על המטבעות, ומשם CH, הונגריה היא מדיארורסאג, פינלנד היא סואומי, נורווגיה היא נורגה ("הדרך צפונה"), יוון היא הלאס, אלבניה היא שקיפריה, קרואטיה היא הרוואטסקה, מונטנגרו היא צרנה גורה ("ההר השחור"), ואירלנד היא אירה.
חלק 2 בפרופיל.

lines.line: Not even Germans. They say Deutschland, from an old word for: of the people.
Austria is Österreich. The eastern realm.
Switzerland has four languages, so four names. On its coins, it's Helvetia. That's why it's C. H.
Hungary? Magyarország. Land of the Magyars.
Finland is Suomi. Even the Finns aren't sure where that comes from.
Next door, Norway is Norge. The way north.
Greece is Hellas. Romans said Graeci. Greeks call themselves Hellenes.
Albania is Shqipëria. Many link it to the eagle on its flag.
Montenegro is Crna Gora. Same meaning: black mountain.
And Ireland is Éire. Ireland literally means: land of Éire.
